en.greeting: Hi! Today is about how your English sounds, not just what it says: setting your tone precisely, keeping one voice, and rewriting one message for very different readers.

steps.title: Tone has dials
steps.text: You can already shift register, choose words for their feeling and decode the polite code. Now: tone as a set of dials you control.
steps.body: **Tone** is your attitude to the reader and the subject. Five dials: **formal ↔ casual**, **warm ↔ cool**, **confident ↔ tentative**, **serious ↔ playful**, **direct ↔ indirect**. The levers: word choice, sentence length, contractions, pronouns (*we / you* or *the company*), **hedges** (*perhaps, just, might*: one is polite, many sound unsure) and punctuation (one *!* is friendly, *!!!* is shouting). **Indonesian trap:** English has no *ya / dong / sih*, so don't replace them with *!!!*.

pairs.en: We are unable to …
pairs.id: formal → We can't … (santai)

pairs.en: Please be advised that …
pairs.id: dingin, berjarak → Thanks for your patience (hangat)

pairs.en: We were wondering if maybe …
pairs.id: ragu-ragu → We recommend … (yakin)

pairs.en: It would be great to have it today.
pairs.id: tidak langsung → Please send it by 3 p.m. (langsung)

pairs.en: Quick heads-up: we've moved the meeting to Thursday!
pairs.id: Info singkat: rapatnya kami pindah ke Kamis! (hangat, santai)

pairs.en: The meeting has been moved to Thursday.
pairs.id: Rapatnya dipindah ke Kamis. (netral, dingin: pasif, tanpa orang)

steps.title: Your turn: find the dial
steps.text: Read Rina's email to a new client and decide which dial is turned too far.

options: Too casual: the contraction makes it sound careless.
Too tentative: so many hedges make her sound unsure of her own quote.
Too playful: it sounds as if she's joking.
question.prompt: Rina emails a new client in Singapore about a quote she's proud of: 'Hi Mr Lim, I was just wondering if you might possibly have had a chance to maybe look at the quote, if that's OK?' What's wrong with the tone?
question.explanation: Count the hedges: **just, wondering, might, possibly, maybe, if that's OK**. One would be polite; six make her sound unsure of her own quote. Better: *Hi Mr Lim, have you had a chance to look at the quote? I'm happy to go through it on a call.* One contraction (*that's*) is normal in a neutral email, and nothing in it is a joke.

steps.title: When tone backfires
steps.text: Polite words can still carry the wrong tone. Two kinds do real damage at work.
steps.body:
**The defensive apology** says *sorry* but takes no responsibility: *sorry you feel …*, *sorry if …*, then *However, as clearly stated …*. A real apology names the problem, owns it and says what you'll do.
**Passive-aggressive phrases** (pasif-agresif: annoyance hidden behind polite words) look polite, but many readers hear the sting. These are tendencies: some people use them innocently, so a careful writer avoids them. The fix: **neutral and specific**, a clear request + a reason.

pairs.en: We're sorry you feel the delivery was slow.
pairs.id: maaf atas perasaanmu, bukan keterlambatannya → defensif

pairs.en: However, as clearly stated on our website, …
pairs.id: membatalkan maaf + 'kamu tidak membaca' → defensif

pairs.en: We're sorry your order was late. That was our mistake.
pairs.id: menyebut masalah + mengakuinya → tulus

pairs.en: As per my last email, …
pairs.id: aku sudah bilang; baca email-mu → pasif-agresif

pairs.en: Just a gentle reminder …
pairs.id: (kedua kalinya / setelah tenggat) kamu terlambat, aku kesal

pairs.en: Not sure if you saw my previous email …
pairs.id: kamu mengabaikanku

pairs.en: As I'm sure you're aware, …
pairs.id: harusnya kamu sudah tahu

pairs.en: Could you send the figures by 3 p.m.? I need them for the board pack.
pairs.id: netral dan spesifik: permintaan + alasan

steps.title: Your turn: read the signal
steps.text: A missed deadline in a Jakarta office. What is Pak Hasan really saying?

options: Nothing extra: it's simply a formal way to say 'in my previous email'.
He's sorry for sending Dimas so many emails.
I've already told you this, and I'm annoyed that I have to repeat it.
question.prompt: On Monday, Pak Hasan asked Dimas to send the sales figures by Wednesday. On Thursday morning he emails: 'Hi Dimas, as per my last email, I need the figures today.' What does 'as per my last email' signal here?
question.explanation: Literally it means 'as I said in my last email', but after a missed deadline readers hear **I already told you, and I'm annoyed**. It's not neutral here: the request is repeated and late. Nothing in it is an apology. A kinder version: *Could you send the figures this morning? I need them for the 2 p.m. meeting.*

steps.title: One voice, precise words
steps.text: Next: the personality of a text, and the words that keep it steady.
steps.body:
**Voice** (suara tulisan) stays the same; **tone** shifts with the situation. A startup app's voice is casual and warm; a bank's is calm and precise. Keep **one voice through the whole text**: a chatty message that suddenly says *hereby*, or a bank letter that suddenly says *Awesome, right?*, sounds as if two people wrote it.
**Precise verbs:** one exact verb beats a weak verb + an adverb, and it tells the mood. **Clichés:** cut them, or replace them with a fact.

pairs.en: Your card's on its way!
pairs.id: Kartumu sedang dikirim! (suara startup: santai, hangat)

pairs.en: Your new card has been sent.
pairs.id: Kartu baru Anda telah dikirim. (suara bank: tenang, tepat)

pairs.en: strolled
pairs.id: berjalan santai sambil menikmati (= walked slowly, relaxed)

pairs.en: trudged
pairs.id: berjalan lambat dengan langkah berat, capek

pairs.en: marched
pairs.id: berjalan dengan langkah tegas dan kuat

pairs.en: whispered
pairs.id: berbisik (= said very quietly)

pairs.en: soared / plunged
pairs.id: melonjak / anjlok (= rose / fell very sharply)

pairs.en: at the end of the day
pairs.id: klise: hapus, atau ganti dengan fakta

steps.title: Your turn: keep the voice
steps.text: Jajan is a food delivery app in Jakarta with a friendly, casual voice.

options: Hey Sari, welcome to Jajan! Your first delivery's on us. Pick something tasty and we'll do the rest.
Hey Sari, welcome to Jajan! Your first delivery's on us. The user is hereby advised that this promotion is subject to availability.
Dear Ms Wulandari, welcome to Jajan. We are pleased to inform you that your first delivery is complimentary. Have fun, yeah?
question.prompt: Which welcome message keeps Jajan's friendly, casual voice all the way through?
question.explanation: The first message stays casual and warm to the end: *Hey*, *delivery's*, *on us*, *we'll do the rest*. The second jumps into legal language (*The user is hereby advised … subject to availability*). The third starts stiff and formal, then ends in slang (*Have fun, yeah?*): two voices in one message.

steps.title: Rhythm: end on the strong word
steps.text: You already vary sentence length. Two more habits give a text a steady rhythm.
steps.body:
**Read it aloud.** Where you run out of breath, split the sentence; where every sentence has the same shape, change one.
**End on the strong word.** The end of a sentence is the spotlight, so don't leave a weak tail there (*to be honest*, *I think*, *as well*, *etc.*): move it to the front or cut it. Finish the paragraph on the point you want remembered.

pairs.en: The results were disappointing, to be honest.
pairs.id: lemah: berakhir pada ekor 'to be honest'

pairs.en: To be honest, the results were disappointing.
pairs.id: kuat: berakhir pada 'disappointing'

pairs.en: In the third quarter, profits fell by forty per cent.
pairs.id: kuat: berakhir pada beritanya (40%)

pairs.en: We need your support, and we need it now.
pairs.id: pengulangan pendek, berakhir pada kata terkuat

steps.title: Your turn: the precise verb
steps.text: A practice short story set in a Surabaya hospital. Choose the verb that carries the mood.

options: strolled
marched
trudged
question.prompt: 'After a twelve-hour shift at the hospital, Sari ___ home through the rain, too tired to lift her umbrella.' Which ONE verb is the most precise?
question.explanation: **Trudged** = walked slowly with heavy steps because you're tired: exactly Sari after twelve hours. **Strolled** is slow too, but relaxed and pleasant: the wrong mood. **Marched** is firm and determined: the wrong energy for someone too tired to lift an umbrella.

steps.title: One message, many readers
steps.text: Last skill: rewriting the same news for very different readers. One practice incident: the payment app BayarKu was down for two hours on Friday.
steps.body: In the register lesson you changed the greeting and the verbs. For a really different reader you change the **content** and its **order**. Ask: **who** reads it and what do they know? What's their **first question**? What must they **do or feel**? **Where** will they read it? Customers need an apology and *your money is safe*; the CEO needs the impact; engineers need the cause; the press needs formal, accountable sentences and a named quote.

pairs.en: Sorry, payments aren't working right now. Your money is safe, and we're fixing it.
pairs.id: pelanggan (notifikasi): Maaf, pembayaran sedang tidak bisa. Uangmu aman, kami sedang memperbaikinya.

pairs.en: Payments were down for two hours on Friday: about 48,000 failed transactions, no money lost.
pairs.id: CEO: Pembayaran mati dua jam hari Jumat: sekitar 48.000 transaksi gagal, tidak ada uang hilang.

pairs.en: Migration 412 locked the transactions table at 19:10; rollback completed at 20:52.
pairs.id: engineer: Migrasi 412 mengunci tabel transaksi pukul 19.10; rollback selesai pukul 20.52.

pairs.en: No customer funds were affected, said CEO Dimas Pratama.
pairs.id: siaran pers: Dana pelanggan tidak terdampak, kata CEO Dimas Pratama.

steps.title: Your turn: choose the reader
steps.text: A coffee chain in Bandung has to raise its membership price. Three versions, three readers.

options: From 1 March, membership revenue is expected to grow by about 20%, with churn projected below 3%.
Thank you for being with us. From 1 March, membership will be Rp 55,000 a month because our coffee and milk costs have risen. Your free birthday drink stays.
Membership price: Rp 55,000 from 1 March. Update the till settings before opening that day.
question.prompt: Kopi Nusantara is raising its membership from Rp 45,000 to Rp 55,000 a month. Which version is written for its loyal members?
question.explanation: Loyal members get **thanks**, the **new price**, an **honest reason** and **what stays the same**, in warm, plain words. The first version talks about revenue and churn (members who leave): that's for investors. The third is an instruction for the staff at the till.

steps.title: Nada punya kenop
steps.text: Kamu sudah bisa menggeser register, memilih kata dari rasanya dan membaca kode sopan. Sekarang: nada sebagai beberapa kenop yang kamu kendalikan.
steps.body: **Nada** (tone) adalah sikapmu terhadap pembaca dan topiknya. Lima kenop: **formal ↔ santai**, **hangat ↔ dingin**, **yakin ↔ ragu-ragu**, **serius ↔ jenaka**, **langsung ↔ tidak langsung**. Tuasnya: pilihan kata, panjang kalimat, bentuk singkat, kata ganti (*we / you* atau *the company*), **pelunak** (*perhaps, just, might*: satu sopan, banyak terdengar ragu) dan tanda baca (satu *!* ramah, *!!!* seperti berteriak). **Jebakan:** bahasa Inggris tidak punya *ya / dong / sih*, jadi jangan menggantinya dengan *!!!*.

steps.title: Giliranmu: temukan kenopnya
steps.text: Baca email Rina untuk klien baru dan tentukan kenop mana yang diputar terlalu jauh.

options: Too casual: the contraction makes it sound careless.
Too tentative: so many hedges make her sound unsure of her own quote.
Too playful: it sounds as if she's joking.
question.prompt: Rina mengirim email ke klien baru di Singapura tentang penawaran harga yang ia banggakan: 'Hi Mr Lim, I was just wondering if you might possibly have had a chance to maybe look at the quote, if that's OK?' Apa masalah nadanya?
question.explanation: Hitung pelunaknya: **just, wondering, might, possibly, maybe, if that's OK**. Satu saja sudah sopan; enam membuatnya terdengar tidak yakin dengan penawarannya sendiri. Lebih baik: *Hi Mr Lim, have you had a chance to look at the quote? I'm happy to go through it on a call.* Satu bentuk singkat (*that's*) wajar di email netral, dan tidak ada candaan di dalamnya.
displayOptions: Terlalu santai: bentuk singkat membuatnya terdengar ceroboh.
Terlalu ragu-ragu: terlalu banyak pelunak membuatnya tidak yakin dengan penawarannya sendiri.

steps.title: Saat nada jadi bumerang
steps.text: Kata-kata sopan tetap bisa membawa nada yang salah. Dua jenis ini benar-benar merusak di tempat kerja.
steps.body:
**Permintaan maaf yang defensif** berkata *sorry* tapi tidak mengambil tanggung jawab: *sorry you feel …*, *sorry if …*, lalu *However, as clearly stated …*. Maaf yang sungguhan menyebut masalahnya, mengakuinya dan mengatakan apa yang akan dilakukan.
**Frasa pasif-agresif** (kesal yang disamarkan kata-kata sopan) tampak sopan, tapi banyak pembaca merasakan sindirannya. Ini kecenderungan: ada yang memakainya tanpa maksud apa-apa, jadi penulis yang cermat menghindarinya. Solusinya: **netral dan spesifik**, permintaan yang jelas + alasan.

steps.title: Giliranmu: baca sinyalnya
steps.text: Tenggat yang terlewat di kantor Jakarta. Sebenarnya apa yang dikatakan Pak Hasan?

options: Nothing extra: it's simply a formal way to say 'in my previous email'.
He's sorry for sending Dimas so many emails.
I've already told you this, and I'm annoyed that I have to repeat it.
question.prompt: Hari Senin, Pak Hasan meminta Dimas mengirim angka penjualan paling lambat hari Rabu. Kamis pagi ia mengirim email: 'Hi Dimas, as per my last email, I need the figures today.' Apa sinyal 'as per my last email' di sini?
question.explanation: Secara harfiah artinya 'seperti yang kusampaikan di email terakhir', tapi setelah tenggat lewat pembaca mendengar **aku sudah bilang, dan aku kesal**. Di sini tidak netral: permintaannya diulang dan sudah terlambat. Tidak ada permintaan maaf di dalamnya. Versi yang lebih ramah: *Could you send the figures this morning? I need them for the 2 p.m. meeting.*

Dia menyesal sudah mengirim terlalu banyak email.
Dia sudah memberi tahu dan kesal harus mengulanginya.

steps.title: Satu suara, kata yang tepat
steps.text: Berikutnya: kepribadian sebuah tulisan, dan kata-kata yang menjaganya tetap stabil.
steps.body:
**Suara** (voice) tetap sama; **nada** (tone) berubah sesuai situasi. Suara aplikasi startup santai dan hangat; suara bank tenang dan tepat. Jaga **satu suara di seluruh tulisan**: pesan santai yang tiba-tiba memakai *hereby*, atau surat bank yang tiba-tiba berkata *Awesome, right?*, terdengar seperti ditulis dua orang.
**Kata kerja yang tepat:** satu kata kerja yang pas lebih baik daripada kata kerja lemah + kata keterangan, dan ia menunjukkan suasananya. **Klise:** buang, atau ganti dengan fakta.

steps.title: Giliranmu: jaga suaranya
steps.text: Jajan adalah aplikasi pesan-antar makanan di Jakarta dengan suara yang ramah dan santai.

options: Hey Sari, welcome to Jajan! Your first delivery's on us. Pick something tasty and we'll do the rest.
Hey Sari, welcome to Jajan! Your first delivery's on us. The user is hereby advised that this promotion is subject to availability.
Dear Ms Wulandari, welcome to Jajan. We are pleased to inform you that your first delivery is complimentary. Have fun, yeah?
question.prompt: Pesan sambutan mana yang menjaga suara Jajan yang ramah dan santai dari awal sampai akhir?
question.explanation: Pesan pertama tetap santai dan hangat sampai akhir: *Hey*, *delivery's*, *on us*, *we'll do the rest*. Pesan kedua melompat ke bahasa hukum (*The user is hereby advised … subject to availability*). Pesan ketiga mulai kaku dan formal, lalu berakhir dengan bahasa gaul (*Have fun, yeah?*): dua suara dalam satu pesan.

steps.title: Ritme: akhiri dengan kata yang kuat
steps.text: Kamu sudah memvariasikan panjang kalimat. Dua kebiasaan lagi membuat ritme tulisan terjaga.
steps.body:
**Bacakan dengan suara keras.** Di mana napasmu habis, pecah kalimatnya; kalau setiap kalimat punya bentuk yang sama, ubah satu.
**Akhiri dengan kata yang kuat.** Akhir kalimat adalah lampu sorot, jadi jangan tinggalkan ekor yang lemah di sana (*to be honest*, *I think*, *as well*, *etc.*): pindahkan ke depan atau buang. Tutup paragraf dengan poin yang ingin diingat.

steps.text: Cerita pendek latihan berlatar rumah sakit di Surabaya. Pilih kata kerja yang membawa suasananya.

question.prompt: 'After a twelve-hour shift at the hospital, Sari ___ home through the rain, too tired to lift her umbrella.' SATU kata kerja mana yang paling tepat?
question.explanation: **Trudged** = berjalan lambat dengan langkah berat karena capek: persis Sari setelah dua belas jam. **Strolled** juga lambat, tapi santai dan menyenangkan: suasananya salah. **Marched** tegas dan bersemangat: energinya salah untuk orang yang terlalu capek untuk mengangkat payung.

steps.title: Satu pesan, banyak pembaca
steps.text: Keterampilan terakhir: menulis ulang berita yang sama untuk pembaca yang sangat berbeda. Satu kejadian latihan: aplikasi pembayaran BayarKu mati dua jam pada hari Jumat.
steps.body: Di pelajaran register kamu mengganti salam dan kata kerjanya. Untuk pembaca yang benar-benar berbeda, kamu mengubah **isi** dan **urutannya**. Tanyakan: **siapa** yang membaca dan apa yang sudah mereka tahu? Apa **pertanyaan pertama** mereka? Apa yang harus mereka **lakukan atau rasakan**? **Di mana** mereka membacanya? Pelanggan perlu maaf dan *your money is safe*; CEO perlu dampaknya; engineer perlu penyebabnya; pers perlu kalimat formal yang bertanggung jawab dan kutipan dari orang yang disebut namanya.

steps.text: Sebuah jaringan kedai kopi di Bandung harus menaikkan harga keanggotaannya. Tiga versi, tiga pembaca.

question.prompt: Kopi Nusantara menaikkan harga keanggotaannya dari Rp 45.000 menjadi Rp 55.000 per bulan. Versi mana yang ditulis untuk anggota setianya?
question.explanation: Anggota setia mendapat **ucapan terima kasih**, **harga baru**, **alasan yang jujur** dan **apa yang tetap sama**, dengan kata-kata yang hangat dan sederhana. Versi pertama membahas pendapatan dan churn (anggota yang berhenti): itu untuk investor. Versi ketiga adalah instruksi untuk staf di kasir.

steps.title: Contekan
steps.text: Kenop nada, frasa yang jadi bumerang, suara, ritme dan pembaca dalam satu halaman.

artifact.title: Contekan · Nuansa gaya
artifact.intro: Atur kenopnya, jaga satu suara, akhiri dengan kuat, dan tulis untuk pembaca yang ada di depanmu.
rows: We are unable to … / We can't …
Thanks for your patience / Please be advised …
pelunak: satu sopan, banyak terdengar ragu
We recommend … / We were wondering if maybe …
a plain fact / a light joke
Please send it by 3 p.m. / It would be great to have it today.
maaf atas perasaan, lalu membela diri
We're sorry you feel … However, as clearly stated …
We're sorry your order was late. We've refunded the fee.
As per my last email … / Just a gentle reminder (again) …
startup: casual, warm · bank: calm, precise
satu kata kerja, bukan kata kerja + keterangan
at the end of the day, think outside the box
bacakan; akhiri dengan kata yang kuat
To be honest, the results were disappointing.
tips: Satu pelunak itu sopan; tiga terdengar ragu. Satu ! ramah; !!! seperti berteriak.
Sebelum mengirim pengingat, hapus 'As per my last email' dan 'gentle': tulis permintaan yang jelas dan alasannya.
Untuk pembaca baru, ubah isi dan urutannya, bukan hanya salamnya.

examples.en: Could you send your timesheet today? Payroll closes at 5 p.m.
examples.id: Bisa kirim timesheet-mu hari ini? Penggajian ditutup pukul 17.00. (netral, bukan pasif-agresif)

examples.en: We're sorry your order arrived five days late. That was our mistake, and we've refunded the delivery fee.
examples.id: Kami minta maaf pesananmu terlambat lima hari. Itu kesalahan kami, dan ongkos kirimnya sudah kami kembalikan. (maaf yang sungguhan)

examples.en: After the night shift, Sari trudged home through the rain.
examples.id: Setelah sif malam, Sari berjalan pulang dengan langkah berat di tengah hujan. (kata kerja yang tepat)

examples.en: In the third quarter, profits fell by forty per cent.
examples.id: Di kuartal ketiga, laba turun empat puluh persen. (berakhir pada kata yang kuat)

steps.title: Baca lebih lanjut
steps.text: Dua bacaan singkat dari penulis profesional: nada sebagai kenop, dan panduan suara dan nada dari sebuah perusahaan.
